nodes.description: A patent document titled "Real-time ad-hoc spam filtering of email" describing a multi-pass ad-hoc spam message filtering approach that dynamically generates a temporary classifier.

A message filter that dynamically generates a temporary classification model during a first pass based on results of a previously applied message filter, then uses the model in a second pass to retrospectively inspect messages and identify possible misclassifications.

A message filter that assigns messages to different message folders and stores first classification data in a persistent store, executed automatically independent of user action.<SEP>A previously applied message filter that sorts messages into various folders for a user and stores first classification data in a persistent store.

A model generated by the multi-pass message filter based on first pass analysis, configured to reside exclusively in a non-persistent memory location and used to score messages for misclassification identification.
Classification data generated by the first message filter and stored in a persistent store.<SEP>Classification data stored in a persistent store by the first message filter.

Classification data generated by the first pass of the multi-pass message filter, residing exclusively in a non-persistent memory store at the client device and deleted upon providing the display of information.<SEP>Classification data generated by the first pass of the multi-pass message filter, configured to reside exclusively in a non-persistent memory store.

A device configured to receive messages, assign them to message folders using the first message filter, and communicate the messages over a network.<SEP>A device comprising a transceiver to send and receive data over a network and a processor operative to perform multi-pass message filtering actions to manage message delivery.

A device that executes passes of the multi-pass message filter, stores second classification data in non-persistent memory, and provides a display of information enabling a user to move identified messages to another message folder.<SEP>A user's device on which the multi-pass message filter passes execute and where the classification model is maintained in memory.
A storage medium including data and instructions that, when executed on a computing device, provide for managing messages via multi-pass filtering.
Different folders into which messages are sorted by the first message filter and inspected by the multi-pass message filter.
A classifier employed by the multi-pass message filter.
An identification of sorted messages that might be misclassified, generated by the second pass and displayed so a user can move misclassified messages to different folders.
A memory-resident-only location where the generated classification model resides, not stored on disk or in another persistent data store, and from which it is purged.
A storage location where the first message filter stores first classification data.<SEP>A persistent data store where the first message filter stores first classification data.

A person enabled to move identified messages to another message folder and able to select execution of the multi-pass message filter through an interface on the client device.<SEP>A person for whom messages are sorted into folders and who is presented a list of possibly misclassified messages to move them to different folders.

A communication item received in plurality, assigned to message folders, scored by the multi-pass message filter, and potentially identified as sorted into an incorrect folder.<SEP>An email message that is sorted into folders, scanned for information such as sender information, headers, subject, originating network address, contents, and attachments, and scored by the multi-pass message filter.
Information within a message identifying the sender, read during the first pass analysis.
Headers within a message, including a subject, read during the first pass analysis.
The network address from which a message originates, read during the first pass analysis.
The content of a message, read during the first pass analysis.
Files attached to a message, read during the first pass analysis.

An address book associated with a recipient that is associated with the message folders, used in analysis for generating second classification data.<SEP>An address book associated with a recipient that is associated with the message folders, used in analysis for generating the classification model.
A component of the network device that sends and receives data over a network.
A component of the network device operative to perform actions including the first and second pass analyses and purging the classification model.

A message filter executed in multiple passes on a client device to train itself by generating second classification data, score each message, and identify messages sorted into incorrect message folders.
A folder into which messages are sorted; a message may be identified as stored into an incorrect message folder and moved to another message folder.
A communications network over which messages are communicated between the network device and the client device.
A memory store at the client device where second classification data resides exclusively.
An interface on the client device through which a user can select execution of the multi-pass message filter.

edges.description: The patent document describes the multi-pass ad-hoc spam message filtering approach.
The multi-pass message filter generates a classification model during the first pass and uses it in the second pass.
The multi-pass message filter generates its classification model based on results of the previously applied first message filter.
The first pass of the multi-pass message filter trains the filter by generating second classification data.
The second pass of the multi-pass message filter generates a misclassification identification of sorted messages.
The network device's processor performs the first and second pass analyses using the multi-pass message filter.
The storage medium includes instructions that enable executing the passes of the multi-pass message filter.
The multi-pass message filter employs a Naive Bayes classifier.
The first and second passes of the multi-pass message filter occur entirely on a client device.
The multi-pass message filter performs first pass analysis on messages and scores each message in the second pass.
The first message filter sorts messages into a plurality of different message folders.
The first message filter is configured to store first classification data in a persistent store.<SEP>The first message filter stores first classification data in a persistent store.
The network device assigns messages to message folders using the first message filter.<SEP>The first message filter is configured to execute on a network device distinct from a client device.
The first message filter assigns messages to a plurality of different message folders.
The generated classification model is configured to reside exclusively in a non-persistent memory location.
The network device purges the generated classification model from the non-persistent memory location.
The classification model is generated based on analysis of whether a message sender's address is in an address book associated with a recipient.
The classification model is generated based on an analysis of at least which message folder a message currently resides.
The first classification data is stored in a persistent store.
The second classification data is configured to reside exclusively in a non-persistent memory store.
The first pass of the multi-pass message filter trains the filter by generating second classification data.
The second classification data resides exclusively in a non-persistent memory store at the client device.
The second classification data is deleted from the client device upon providing the display of information.
The second classification data is generated based on analysis including a message sender's address in an address book associated with a recipient.
The second classification data is generated based on which folder each of the plurality of messages resides.
The network device comprises a transceiver to send and receive data over a network.
The network device comprises a processor operative to perform the filtering actions.
The network device receives a plurality of messages and communicates them over the network to the message folders.
The network device communicates messages over the network.
The multi-pass message filter is executed on the client device in multiple passes.
The client device communicates over the network with the network device.
The client device provides a display of information enabling a user to move identified messages to another message folder.
The interface is located on the client device.
The user is enabled to move identified misclassified messages to another message folder.
Messages are sorted into a plurality of different message folders.
The misclassification identification is displayed to the user so misclassified messages can be moved to different folders.
The user is enabled to move the identified message to another message folder.
The user can select execution of the multi-pass message filter through an interface on the client device.
Messages contain sender information read during the first pass analysis.
Messages contain headers, including a subject, read during the first pass analysis.
Messages contain an originating network address read during the first pass analysis.
Messages contain contents read during the first pass analysis.
Messages contain attachments read during the first pass analysis.
The second pass of the multi-pass message filter scores each message and identifies messages sorted into an incorrect message folder.
Messages are sorted into message folders and may be identified as stored into an incorrect message folder.
